name: Eddie Jacobs
caption: Won the N.E.W. Intercontinental Championship in a Crucifix Match, then retained it against a challenger who turned on his own stable to join Jacobs's.

tenures.role: wrestler — N.E.W. Intercontinental Champion; leader of Too Extreme (2EX)
tenures.note: Won the N.E.W. Intercontinental Championship from Balial in a Crucifix Match at King of the Mat 2 (6 April 1998), aided from outside by stablemate Jim Whitten. Defended against Ian Walsh at Friday Night Slam Dance (24 April 1998) in a match that ended without a finish when Walsh turned on his own New Wave Society stable to join Jacobs's Too Extreme (2EX).
Introduced as one half of a new tag team with Nevada Harris ahead of their first televised match together.

tenures.source: the promotion's own closing pay-per-view weekend (19-21 March 1999)
tenures.note: Won the Northeast Heritage Championship from Tony Houston on the first night of the closing pay-per-view weekend (19 March 1999); lost it to Mr. Apples the following night, 20 March 1999; eliminated second (by Andrew Tucker) from the promotion's own final four-way elimination match for the World Heavyweight Championship on its last night, 21 March 1999.
Lost SuperBout VII to "Bad Eye" McBaine in a bloody brawl that began when the two men crashed a van through the arena entrance.

tenures.source: Billed for the second night on the event's own lineup of 2 June 2002; the event was called off before it was held.

name: Balial
caption: Lost the N.E.W. Intercontinental Championship after being tied to a suspended crucifix.

name: Steve Miller
caption: N.E.W. North American Champion, and the presidential faction's own spokesman for its rebrand from the Fellas to the Fab Five.

tenures.note: Already N.E.W. Retained against Drew Snyder at King of the Mat 2 (6 April 1998) with help from an ally known only as the Masked Man. At Friday Night Slam Dance (24 April 1998), delivered the belt shot that let stablemate Vinny Vitrone win the N.E.W. Heavyweight Championship, then announced the stable's rebrand from the Fellas to the Fab Five.

name: Drew Snyder
caption: Came up short challenging for the N.E.W. North American Championship after outside interference twice turned the match.

identity.note: The registry's own 'drew-snyder-uiw-aol' (Ultimate Impact Wrestling, an AOL-hosted fed, 1996-97) shares the bare name only — no moniker, operator, or roster document ties the two, and no aka is recorded on either row.

tenures.note: Challenged Steve Miller for the N.E.W. North American Championship at King of the Mat 2 (6 April 1998); the match was restarted once after an initial disqualification finish, then decided when an unmasked ally of Miller's, the Masked Man, clipped Snyder's knee from outside.

name: Ashli Silver
caption: Wrestled Poison Kiss to a no-finish in a Tuxedo Match after a manager's interference ended it early.

tenures.note: Wrestled Poison Kiss in a Women's Tuxedo Match at King of the Mat 2 (6 April 1998); the match ended without a fall after Steve Miller's manager Monica interfered.

name: Poison Kiss
caption: Wrestled Ashli Silver to a no-finish in a Tuxedo Match after a manager's interference ended it early.

tenures.note: Wrestled Ashli Silver in a Women's Tuxedo Match at King of the Mat 2 (6 April 1998); the match ended without a fall after Steve Miller's manager Monica interfered.

name: Patty Babes Carter
caption: Challenged for the N.E.W. Heavyweight Championship at King of the Mat 2 after turning on his own former friend.

identity.note: The registry already carries two other 'Patty Babes Carter' rows, both RSPWF Top 200 poll stubs with no tenure this record could date (patty-babes-carter-rspwf, tagged SJPW; patty-babes-carter-bwa, tagged BWA) — the name is distinctive, but no operator, moniker beyond the bare name, or roster document ties either to this promotion's own billing.

tenures.note: Formerly Assaf Levavy's own friend and a second referee in an earlier cage match between Levavy and James Pillow, until turning on Levavy; hired Ronnie Whiplash as an ally afterward. Challenged Levavy for the N.E.W. Heavyweight Championship at King of the Mat 2 (6 April 1998) and lost.

name: Tank
caption: A New Revolution wrestler beaten by a New Wave Society rival with a smuggled pair of brass knuckles.

identity.note: 'Tank' is a generic archetype ring name; the registry's own bare 'tank' and 'cwfpro-tank' rows share the name only, with no operator, moniker, or roster document tying either to this promotion's own billing.

tenures.role: wrestler — member of the New Revolution
tenures.note: Billed from New York State. Lost to GlacierIce at Friday Night Slam Dance (24 April 1998) after New Wave Society stablemate 'the Iceman' Chris Lethbridge passed GlacierIce a pair of brass knuckles; the match had briefly been called for Tank by an early bell, then restarted.

name: GlacierIce
caption: A New Wave Society wrestler who beat Tank with help from a smuggled pair of brass knuckles.

tenures.role: wrestler — member of the New Wave Society (NwS)
tenures.note: Billed from Juneau, Alaska. Beat Tank at Friday Night Slam Dance (24 April 1998) after stablemate 'the Iceman' Chris Lethbridge slipped him a pair of brass knuckles.

name: Apocalypse
caption: Teamed with Vinny Vitrone in a losing N.E.W. Tag Team Championship tournament final, then turned on his own partner mid-match.

identity.note: 'Apocalypse' is a generic archetype ring name carried by at least a dozen other registered, unrelated characters (including apocalypse-inwi, a 1997 INWI wrestler); this wing's own text narrates a general shared roster between N.E.W. and INWI, but no moniker, operator, or roster document ties this specific billing to any one of the existing Apocalypse rows, so this pass mints fresh rather than presuming a match on the bare archetype name alone.

tenures.note: Teamed with Vinny Vitrone in the N.E.W. Tag Team Championship Tournament final at King of the Mat 2 (6 April 1998); chokeslammed and powerbombed his own partner mid-match after a dispute, leaving the Crash Test Dummies to win the titles.

name: "The Show Stopper" Scott Jamison
caption: A September 1998 N.E.W. newcomer, living six months a year in a Las Vegas presidential suite, who says he is "Not Hot" yet and that "The New Wave of the N.E.W. has arrived".
notes: Known from one roleplay posted to rec.sport.pro-wrestling.fantasy (msg_id DDKwzojB1qoJ, 10 September 1998), served at /promotions/rspwf/archive/scott-jamison-roleplay-what-do-you-think-1998-09-10.html. In his MGM Grand suite with valet Tammi Winters, he compares himself to Kobe Bryant, says he was labelled 'the next Ivan Ramius', and looks ahead to a Friday match with Tim Warren after a close loss to John Smith. The N.E.W. (1996 to 2000) is the held wing named by the roleplay.

tenures.source: /promotions/rspwf/archive/scott-jamison-roleplay-what-do-you-think-1998-09-10.html (the roleplay names the federation; dated by the post)
The promotion's own second pay-per-view (26 June 1999) and its own 7 July 1999 broadcast.

identity.note: Shares a bare ring name with 1 held record; no card, operator, roster or text ties this post's character to any of them, so they are filed distinct.

name: Supersonic
notes: Known from one sample roleplay posted to rec.sport.pro-wrestling.fantasy on 13 November 1998, titled "[Sample Roleplay] Supersonic", served at /promotions/rspwf/archive/sample-roleplay-supersonic-1998-11-13.html, written for the N.E.W.: a rookie of six foot two and 234 pounds who reveals himself in the control room of "On The Spot" in a sleeveless black Nike T-shirt, tells Nick Demola and "Da Greatest Ever" Shawn Walsh that he is the fed's future and will beat both at Born Again, compares Demola to a bulldog and himself to a wolf, and says he lost to Demola in a parking lot match at Tag Team Hell.
caption: A 234-pound N.E.W. rookie who promises to beat Nick Demola and Shawn Walsh at Born Again in November 1998.
